title: More the Merrier
synopsis: Your in-laws, three exes, a missionary cousin, and an estranged sibling all confirm for Thanksgiving. You have one oven and one nerve left. Cook.

nodes.text: You finalize the guest list. Twenty. The oven is, by spec, sufficient for fifteen.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honest—follows you into whatever comes next.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Hospitable—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Your estranged sister Anita confirms. She has not been to a family event in seven years. Your stomach drops.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Reach.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Quiet—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Your spouse's ex confirms because their kids' custody schedule landed here. You agree, reluctantly, because the kids are great.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Strategic.
“Let it be casual” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Trust.

nodes.text: Your cousin Joel has flown in from Cambodia and would like to give a 'short prayer.' Short, for Joel, is twenty minutes.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Pre-negotiate the prayer.” The story records the instinct as “Strategic” and carries it forward.
“Let Joel be Joel” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Mercy.

nodes.text: Mom would like, again, the green bean casserole. She would also like it on her plate. She has opinions.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Honor—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Risk.

nodes.text: You go to the grocery store and discover that 3 p.m. on the Tuesday before Thanksgiving is, somehow, both apocalypse and prom.

choices.consequence: “Make a list” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Discipline.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Speed.

nodes.text: Anita leaves a voicemail. 'I'm bringing Steve,' she says. Steve is, as far as you know, the man she was supposed to marry seven years ago.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Welcome Steve” back. Grace shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Ask if you're sure.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Your spouse is, professionally, fine. Personally, your spouse is melting. You realize you have been only managing logistics.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Care—follows you into whatever comes next.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Sched.

nodes.text: The math, finally done, is: two ovens. One toaster oven. One spatchcock turkey. Two hours and forty minutes start to finish.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Spatchcock it” back. Aggressive shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Buy a second small turkey.” The story records the instinct as “Easier” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You make pies on Tuesday night because Wednesday is going to be hellish. The crust is, mercifully, good.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Generous.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Pragmatic—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Anita arrives Wednesday with Steve, a houseplant, and a kind smile. She hugs you in the driveway. You realize you have been wrong about seven years of something.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Hug her back fully.” The story records the instinct as “Repair” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Welcome her warmly but cautiously.” The story records the instinct as “Pace” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Your in-laws arrive. They have brought, again, the wrong wine. The wrong wine is, technically, very nice.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Open the wine” back. Generous shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You commit to “Save it for Christmas.” The story records the instinct as “Strategic” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Five children, ages 3-12, are now in the house. The 12-year-old has decided, today, to be a vegetarian.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Easy.
There is no taking “Add a vegetarian main” back. Hospitable shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: 5:30 a.m. The turkey goes in. You make coffee. The kitchen window goes gold.

choices.text: Sit at the window for ten minutes
choices.consequence: “Sit at the window for ten minutes” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Calm.
There is no taking “Start the next thing” back. Move shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Mom and your spouse have a brief, vicious exchange about the green bean casserole. Anita is the one who, somehow, fixes it.

choices.consequence: “Thank Anita publicly later” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Honor.
“Just be grateful” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Quiet.

nodes.text: You give the toast. You decide, in the moment, what kind of family you'd like this to be.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Brave.
There is no taking “Be sweet and short” back. Mercy shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Joel's prayer is, mercifully, only six minutes. He blesses Anita and Steve specifically. Anita cries.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Hold her hand” back. Family shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

choices.text: Pretend not to notice the tear
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Mercy—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: The meal is, somehow, on time. The turkey is, somehow, juicy. The casserole, finally, is on Mom's plate. She does not, however, say thank you. She doesn't have to.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Win.
You commit to “Refill the wine.” The story records the instinct as “Hospitable” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Your spouse's ex tells a small joke. Everyone laughs. The kids, for one beautiful minute, treat their two-household family as a one-table family.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Notice it.” The story records the instinct as “Witness” and carries it forward.
“Just let it be” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Trust.

nodes.text: Anita does dishes with you. You and she talk for an hour about nothing important and everything important. Seven years closes.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Invite her for Christmas.” The story records the instinct as “Continue” and carries it forward.

choices.text: Take it one holiday at a time
choices.consequence: “Take it one holiday at a time” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Slow.

nodes.text: Late. House half-asleep. You and your spouse cut the last pie at midnight at the kitchen island.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Eat the pie together.” The story records the instinct as “Marriage” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Save it for tomorrow” back. Discipline shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: Anita comes for Christmas. Then Easter. Then everything. The family is, somehow, both bigger and easier. Mom, eventually, asks for Anita's casserole recipe.
Next year you do a smaller Thanksgiving on purpose — just the immediate house and Anita and Steve. It is, by every measurement, more fun and less hot.

Years later you compile a small family recipe book. Mom's casserole is on page two. Joel's overlong prayer is, somehow, a chapter. Anita writes the introduction. You all laugh at it on Thanksgivings to come.
